author: @RylanStorm
text:
I had a very honest conversation with the dealer after purchasing my Seal AWD Excellence. In the UK, BYDs are typically co-located with Peugeot or Vauxhall dealerships and he was coming from the Peugeot dealership next door.  His main comment was that the biggest hurdle with the BYD cars is the fact it's a Chinese car and there are a lot of people who just cannot get over the idea that it's a cheap knock-off of a Tesla.  The result is that they get far less visitors than the Peugeot but sales are higher because the conversion rate is much higher.  Once people get into the showroom they've already moved past that "Chinese Car Stigma" and the car just sells itself. 

I got a pre-reg car registered in November. It was £10k lower than list price and is costing me less than £400 a month including maintenance.

author: @TheVirtualAirlinePilot
text:
Wow!   Don't really know how I landed on this video, but as a person who has received specialist training and loves to drive anywhere and everywhere (can't remember when I last took a bus or train!), I decided to watch your review all the way through.  I actually never knew that BYD was  car maker!!

Ok, my thoughts . . . as a Mercedes C Class petrol C180 Elegance driver (it's 20 years old, Petrol with 185,000 on the clock, but it goes so well), I have always said no to electric cars.   Why?  Ok I would want one that fulfils certain conditions that not one EV comes close to - yet.;   At least a 420 mile range with a 15 mile reliable reserve (note that ALL manufacturers overstate their vehicle ranges !!).   Milage - yeah, 323 miles, I don't think so.   I wonder what the driving conditions and speeds were for you to get 200 miles out of it? A decent cockpit too!   Having just returned from a holiday in the US, my rental car was like driving the bloody Space Shuttle!   Why can't manufacturers just do a good, simple instrument panel?   It took me ages to figure out how to start the car, select the lights, wipers and Air Con - and I never worked out the cruise control!   All this on a normal petrol car, just so much easier on the Merc!   

And I am dead against having a bloody laptop in the front driving area!!    Yes, all those fancy things are all well and good, but IMHO dangerous!   There was a time when having a "screen" in front was illegal!   If they are going to encourage people to switch to EV's then this sort of vehicle could really confuse the older generation who can still drive well and safely.   Lane assist?   Terrible idea!   I want to have a car that "I" drive, not have it drive for me.   As a specialist trained driver, I want to be in full control.   I had this on the US Rental car and it was a nightmare on the freeways!  I am happy to have things that are useful to me.   One really great utility on the rental car, was that it had small lights in the wing mirrors that alerted you when a car was really close (they pass on both sides on the freeways in the US!)  

Ok, don't get me wrong.   If I could find a car that meets all my wants then I would happily switch!   Maybe this car is a candidate?   But I would want to make sure that certain "assists" could be disabled before I took delivery.   I am very glad you are happy with this car.   The driving seat position also looks really good.   But I'm not sure I would be tempted to buy this yet.   I am waiting for seriously big improvements in range, battery life and overall usefulness, since in these cars, the battery powers everything;  Lights, Music, Air Con and all things electric - and it also has to power the drive train.   My Merc has a battery for all these electrical things and petrol drives the engine, so the engine can still run if the battery suddenly dies.

And £45700 for this?  Well surprise, surprise for an EV, I was quite astonished as it's a really competitive price for this vehicle!   EV's over 50 grand are not as feature rich as this car appears to be.   Oh, one other matter.   Keyless entry?  No thanks!   Real security risk!   Thieves now have the ability to electronically get into a keyless car and steal it away in under 15 seconds.   Coming from 38 years in the Security industry, I know how bad this is getting to be.

So, you got my attention and thanks for the review.   Very glad you possibly found the car you really want?   Let's hope they give you a good deal.   I will get rid of the Merc one day and I will look more closely at BYD.   All the best to you.   Lee (virtualairlinepilot.org)

author: @GrumpyBulb
text:
I changed from a Tesla M3 LR to a BYD Seal Excellence 5k miles ago & few observations:

Negatives:
I've never seen the claimed 0-60 in 3.8s, it is always, always, always 4.2s regardless of soc or weather conditions. 0.4s is quite a big difference from the claimed performance which is disappointing.
The accelerator pedal feels muted, even in Sport. You mash the pedal & it feels like an internal combustion engine rising in revs & torque. The Tesla (& Polestar) I've previously owned had instant response to pedal inputs, ultimately that's not really an issue but the real issue is when you lift off the accelerator pedal, it doesn't stop accelerating at the same time as you lift your foot, it will continue to accelerate for a fraction of a second longer than you want. That fraction of a second feels longer when you're expecting the car to slow as soon as you lift your foot.
The front parking sensors are a waste of time. They only actually work if you drive forwards towards the object then select reverse to activate the front sensors. I've reported this to BYD & apparently this is a feature which is working as intended - total waste of time! Every car I've had for the last 15 years at least had front parking sensors that activated automatically when driving forwards slowly.
The latest UI update is much better except now on the main screen there is so much wasted space that could be filled with widgets / tiles
A/C in the summer isnt as cold as any other car I've owned since I can remember
On average for mixed m/way (70mph) & city driving I struggle to get 3miles/kW - the Tesla returned 4.2m/kW & was regulary drove at 80+mph on m/ways (I cant drive at that speed now because my range in the BYD falls off a cliff!
The drivers seat is not very comfy - under leg support needs increasing & the seat length needs increasing slightly to provide support to the lower part of my thighs (I'm only 5' 8")
The volume of the stereo is woefully low - I can have a conversation with my passenger whilst talking loudly (not shouting) when the volume is at 39 (max). For a claimed 750W system it is appalling, I cant understand why Dynaudio would allow their name to be associated with a poorly performing product
Rear view camera is pointless when driving in the wet, it is positioned to collect all the spray & crap off the road perfectly

Positives:
Build quality & materials are much better than most vehicles especially considering the price of the Seal
The interior of the Seal is a very nice place to be (with exception of the drivers seat on longer journeys) - very very quiet even at m/way speeds
The driver aids are not very intrusive & are easily turned off (speed limit warning) if you prefer. The Lane Departure Warning is probably the best designed on the Seal, it is probably the best version I have experienced in any other car
It looks pretty (in my opinion)
It has a relaxed but responsive chassis (not as hard / twitchy as the Tesla), it reminds me a lot of my old Volvo S90 for ride quality (that is a compliment)

author: @rod2508
text:
I have owned the perfoirmance for roughly 2 months, aside from the battery/distance milage (I came from a standard ICE car with nearly 800km range), its an amazingly good car.
The performance has insane levels of torque, great to leaving people at traffic lights in the dust (without even breaking speed limits). I typically run the car in ECO but the sports mode is next level sports car enthusiast.
The interior is great. Highly reccomend the full leather. The boot space is great. The new sunroof has an electric shade so you dont have to worry about heat.
I heard a lot of people complain about the sound system but it just required a few tweaks and I still cant play it at full volume without hurting my ears. 
Recharge on 7kw single phase takes about 8 hours from 30% to 100% (assuming you run it down like I do and thats almost a week of to and from work). From 30% to 100% on 75kw at the local DC charging station is about 30min. This would be substantially less if there was a local DC charger that could do 150kw but I live in a more regional area and not in the city. I guess eventually the infrastructure will catch up. I just use the time to go shopping and come back to a full car.
Prices? Well I went from a petrol  v6 that was costing me around $100-$120 a week. Now I'm pulling around $30 a week on the public charger (which would be less half that if I had a  7kw charge port installed at house). The price goes up to about $45 at a DC charger (higher fees per kW). Needless to say that for a car that weighs over 500kg more than the previous petrol sedan, I'm very impressed.
Oh I live in Australia too.

text: Hi Nic, great review as always. I've got the same model in white, had it for about a year. I love mine too. The saloon boot is the biggest negative for me, but that's no fault of the car, its big enough for a family of 4 most of the time. Love the fact the child-locks are controllable from the drivers door too, very handy. Also, eco mode can be useful - not just to extend the range, it dampens the throttle response (nothing you can't do in 'Normal'), but has been useful if ferrying people around that are more sensitive to faster acceleration. Makes it easier to have a lighter foot. Great review of a great car.

text:
Or people need to learn that it was never designed as a guaranteed range, it is done in a lab under specific conditions so as to remove outside variables such as temp/weather/speed/driving style, it is purely as a comparison tool to compare the range of car A to car B
If car A has a WLTP of 400km and Car B has a WLTP of 500km, car B will drive further than car A

WLTP is also not an EV thing, it was designed for comparing ranges of ICE cars, which is also where the test is flawed as it is run from 100% till the EV stops, which is often below 0% and that buffer varies from car to car

My thought is that they should have done EVs with maybe 90% highway, 10% city so as to understate range, people will be happy if they buy a car expecting 400km but get 500km, falls under the saying under promise over deliver

Likely wireless charging is 10w. And you said you use Carplay religiously. Iphones and many Android phones are not thermally well designed to handle Carplay/AA while wireless charging. So you end up not seeing your phone charged and it heating up like coal. Try putting your phone on the wireless charger without carplay turned on (disable it from phone) and you will see that it slowly charges.

Same issue is for many car manufacturers as the old wireless standard is 10w.
